title: The store, from scratch
objective: Understand what a zustand store actually is — a closure over a state value and a Set of listeners — and how set/get/subscribe work, with zero React involved.

quiz.prompt: You call `set({ a: 1 })` on a store whose state is `{ a: 0, b: { x: 1 } }`. What is the resulting state?

options.text: { a: 1 } — set replaces the whole state.
{ a: 1, b: { x: 1 } } — top-level merge keeps b untouched.

quiz.prompt: An action does `state.count++` directly and never calls set. What do subscribers see?

options.text: They all fire because the value changed.

quiz.prompt: This action should add a bear, but subscribers never update. Which line is the bug?
quiz.instruction: Return { buggyLine: <1-based line number>, fix: <how to fix it> }.

quiz.prompt: Put the steps of a single `set(updater)` call in order.

items.text: Check Object.is(nextState, state) — bail out if equal
Run the updater function against the current state to get nextState

quiz.instruction: Return the keys as an array in the correct order.
